newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Nursing home review policy offered - Times.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Nursing home review policy offered - Times.

text.p: The Clinton administration is proposing changes in inspections of nursing homes that care for Medicare and Medicaid patients in order to focus on problem areas, the New York Times reported Tuesday.

The proposed changes would allow officials to concentrate on nursing homes that have problems and do not comply with federal standards, according to Department of Health and Human Services documents. The Times said the documents were sent to federal and state health officials.

Government data show more than two-thirds of the nation's nursing homes fall below federal standards, the paper said. Under the proposed changes, reviews at many nursing homes would be narrower in scope; fewer residents would be interviewed and fewer medical records would be examined.
Inspectors would focus on so-called areas of concern rather than more comprehensive reviews in order to increase the efficiency and effectiveness of the inspections, it said.

State officials and consumer groups criticised the proposed changes, saying they would weaken the protections of nursing home residents. One official said the changes would permit cursory, "drive-by surveys."

Nursing homes must meet federal standards to be paid under the government's Medicare and Medicaid programmes. Some $80 billion is spent each year on the care of 1.6 million people in more than 17,000 nursing homes, the newspaper said. On average, nursing homes must be inspected once a year.
